name: Cpl. Wim Daelmans
cause: firing squad, for desertion of post
summary: Conscript corporal. Left his listening post during a bombardment; convicted by field court-martial. The file attributes the loss of the post and eleven men to his absence.

entries.text: Deserted his post under fire, in breach of his oath.
Post No. 9 overrun in his absence; eleven men killed.
Stole rations from the company store.
Wrote letters home for comrades who could not write.
Conscripted at nineteen; did not volunteer.

hidden.text: Left his post to carry a wounded enemy boy to the aid station.

archive.title: Court-martial minutes, Varn Ridge
cards: 3 March, 4 p.m.: Cpl. W. Daelmans placed under arrest, pending field court.
5 March, dawn: Post No. 9 overrun. Held by Pte. Aske and ten relief men.
Finding: desertion of post, 3 March. Sentence: death. Minuted after lunch.

archive.title: Aid-station admission book
cards: No. 3 Aid Station, 3 March, 2.40 p.m.: one enemy soldier, aged about fifteen.
Shrapnel, left thigh. 'Carried in by Cpl Daelmans, who would not give his post.'
Remarks: patient survived; sent to the prisoners' hospital, 9 March.

fact.text: He was under arrest two days before Post No. 9 fell.
He left the post to carry a wounded enemy boy to the aid station.

questions.text: Why did you leave the post?
answer: I said at the trial. Nobody wrote it down. They'd already had lunch.
questions.card: Says he explained at the trial; nobody wrote it down.

answer: There was a lad in the wire. Theirs. Calling for his mother. Same word, near enough.
I couldn't listen to it for another hour, so I went and got him.
questions.card: Went into the wire for an enemy lad calling for his mother.

questions.text: Eleven men died at your post.
answer: Two days after they locked me up. I knew eight of them.
I've done the sum every way there is. I still don't know if I'd have made it twelve or none.
questions.card: Knew eight of the eleven. Can't say if he'd have made it twelve or none.

heaven: A man of about thirty-five, with a limp and a foreign accent, keeps a standing enquiry at the Gilt Gate.
It asks after a corporal. It is finally closed.
hell: The Wardens accept him for the oath alone.
The eleven are struck from his account; nobody thinks to tell him.

ext.mitigating: Age; conscription; the deaths charged to him happened while he was in custody.
